title: Homotopy invariance under concatenation of relative zigzag words
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,W)$ be a category with a wide subcategory, and use the small diagram categories $Z_w(a,b)$, nerves and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]; no homotopy calculus is assumed. Restrict to words in $+,-$. Let $u,v$ be nonempty words with the same first letter and the same last letter. Suppose $F_{a,b}:Z_u(a,b)\to Z_v(a,b)$ is a family of functors, strictly natural in both endpoints for their $W$-actions, and $NF_{a,b}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $a,b$. The endpoint actions are composition: a first $+$ is contravariant in the source, a first $-$ covariant; a last $+$ is covariant in the target, a last $-$ contravariant. For any words $p,q$, including empty words, and any $x,y$, replacing the $u$-subdiagram by $F$ and retaining $p,q$ gives a functor
$$Z_{puq}(x,y)\longrightarrow Z_{pvq}(x,y).$$
Its nerve is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 9.4 and Corollary 9.6, printed pp. 31-32 (PDF pp. 15-16), applied successively at the two cuts of a concatenated word. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Fix $p,q,x,y$ and the family $F$. All categories used below are small after the universe enlargement in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]: their objects and morphisms are finite diagrams in the chosen small category. Let $P=P_p(x)$ have objects the $p$-diagrams whose initial vertex is $x$ and whose final vertex $a$ is allowed to vary; morphisms are commuting vertical $W$-maps, identity only at $x$. Evaluation at the last vertex is a functor $t:P\to W$. Define $Q=Q_q(y)$ similarly using $q$-diagrams with variable initial vertex $b$, fixed final vertex $y$, and evaluation $s:Q\to W$ at the initial vertex. Identity and composition are defined vertexwise. If $p$ is empty, $P$ is the one-object identity category at $x$; if $q$ is empty, $Q$ is the one-object identity category at $y$. These are auxiliary categories explicitly constructed here, not extra hypotheses.

source.place: Section 5.1 and Example 9.3; auxiliary diagram categories with one free endpoint

proof.text: First fix an arbitrary target $b$ and suppose the common first letter of $u,v$ is $-$. The source action is covariant: for $w:a\to a'$ in $W$, $w_!$ replaces the first arrow $a\leftarrow c$ by $a'\xleftarrow{w\circ h}c$. It changes no other vertex or arrow. Thus $D_u:P\to\mathrm{Cat}$, $A\mapsto Z_u(tA,b)$, is a functor; define $D_v$ likewise. By the definition of $\operatorname{Th}$ in [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison], gluing defines an isomorphism $\operatorname{Th}_P D_u\cong Z_{pu}(x,b)$. Indeed a morphism is uniquely a prefix morphism $\alpha:A\to A'$ with endpoint $w=t\alpha$, and a fixed-endpoint morphism $w_!U\to U'$ in $Z_u(tA',b)$. Its first square is precisely the original seam square $w\circ h=h'\circ k$, where $k$ is the next vertical map; all remaining squares are unchanged. Restricting a full diagram gives the inverse correspondence. Vertexwise composition agrees with Grothendieck composition, since composing endpoint maps composes the first arrow and all other vertical maps compose vertexwise. The same identification holds for $v$. Strict naturality of $F$ in the source gives a natural transformation $D_u\to D_v$. Under these identifications its induced functor is exactly replacement by $F$ on the $u$-part, retaining the prefix.

source.place: Proposition 9.4; covariant source case, expanded by the one-sided construction of Example 9.2

proof.text: If the common first letter is $+$, source composition is contravariant: $w^*$ replaces $a'\xrightarrow{h'}c'$ by $a\xrightarrow{h'\circ w}c'$. Now $D_u:P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ sends $A$ to $Z_u(tA,b)$. The definition of $\operatorname{Gr}$ in [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison] gives $\operatorname{Gr}_{P^{\mathrm{op}}}D_u\cong Z_{pu}(x,b)$. Its morphism over $\alpha:A\to A'$ in $P$ is a fiber morphism $U\to w^*U'$ at $tA$, where $w=t\alpha$. The first-square equation is $k\circ h=h'\circ w$, exactly the seam equation in the full diagram. Restriction and gluing are inverse on objects and morphisms and respect vertexwise composition. The same holds for $v$; strict source naturality again gives a natural transformation whose total functor is the desired replacement. In either first-letter case every component is $F_{tA,b}$, a nerve weak homotopy equivalence by hypothesis. The last assertion of [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison], using $P$ with $\operatorname{Th}$ in step 2 or $P^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Gr}$ here, therefore proves that the replacement $F^p_{x,b}:Z_{pu}(x,b)\to Z_{pv}(x,b)$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence for every $b$. The base category is the same on both sides; no assumption about its homotopy type or about endpoint transport being a weak equivalence is required.

source.place: Proposition 9.4 and Corollary 9.6, first cut; homotopy-invariance consequence of the existing Thomason node

proof.text: The family $F^p_{x,b}$ is strictly natural in $b$ for the common last-letter action. On objects, composing a target $W$-map into the last arrow of the $u$-part before or after applying $F$ agrees by the assumed strict target naturality of $F$; the prefix is unchanged. On a full morphism, the source-seam factorization in step 2 or 3 is preserved by that target action, because composition at the two endpoints commutes. For a one-letter $+$ word $h:a\to b$, source precomposition by $w:a_0\to a$ and target postcomposition by $z:b\to b_1$ give $(z\circ h)\circ w=z\circ(h\circ w)$. For a one-letter $-$ word $h:b\to a$, source postcomposition by $w:a\to a_1$ and target precomposition by $z:b_0\to b$ give $(w\circ h)\circ z=w\circ(h\circ z)$. For longer words the actions change separate boundary arrows. On vertical morphisms the interior maps are unchanged. A fixed-target last square $h=h'\circ k$ for $+$ becomes $z\circ h=(z\circ h')\circ k$ after postcomposition; a square $k\circ h=h'$ for $-$ becomes $k\circ(h\circ z)=h'\circ z$ after precomposition. Each follows by associativity. Thus target composition preserves the fiber morphisms and their source-seam factorizations in both cases. The same naturality equality holds on the fixed-endpoint fiber morphism by the hypothesis on $F$. Thus the replacements agree on every vertex and vertical arrow, proving equality of functors, rather than just a natural isomorphism. The words $pu,pv$ remain nonempty and have the same last letter.

source.place: Example 9.3 and naturality in Section 9.1; compatibility needed for the second cut

proof.text: Put $r=pu$ or $pv$ and use the suffix category $Q$ of step 1. If the common last letter is $+$, define $E_r:Q\to\mathrm{Cat}$ by $B\mapsto Z_r(x,sB)$, with covariant target action $w_!$ composing $w:b\to b'$ after the last forward arrow. Gluing identifies $\operatorname{Th}_Q E_r$ with $Z_{rq}(x,y)$: a full morphism uniquely consists of a suffix morphism $\beta:B\to B'$ and a fiber morphism $w_!R\to R'$, $w=s\beta$. For final arrows $h:c\to b$, $h':c'\to b'$ and preceding vertical map $k:c\to c'$, its last-square equation is $w\circ h=h'\circ k$. If the common last letter is $-$, use $E_r:Q^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_{Q^{\mathrm{op}}}E_r$: the target action $w^*$ precomposes the last backward arrow $h':b'\to c'$ by $w$, and the fiber morphism is $R\to w^*R'$ with equation $k\circ h=h'\circ w$. These equations are exactly the seam squares of the full zigzag in the two cases. Restriction and gluing are inverse, and composition agrees by associativity and vertexwise composition. By step 4 the family $F^p$ gives a natural transformation of these diagrams; its component at $B$ is $F^p_{x,sB}$, which is a nerve weak homotopy equivalence by step 3. Apply the last assertion of [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison] over $Q$ or $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ respectively. The resulting total functor retains $p$ and $q$ and applies $F$ to the intervening part, so it is the functor in the statement and its nerve is a weak homotopy equivalence. When a surrounding word is empty the corresponding base is the terminal category described in step 1, and the same identifications and argument apply.

source.place: Proposition 9.4 and Corollary 9.6, second cut; explicit covariant and contravariant target cases
